To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

children with high CP and high CU traits (i) show low startle responses to mental images of fearful situations (i.e. low fear), (ii) show low behavioral inhibition, and (iii) show low sensitivity to punishment.

Children with high/stable conduct problems and high CU traits (i. e. receiving the DSM-5 specifier of Limited Prosocial Emotions) show high startle reactivity, high behavioral inhibition to fear, and low sensitivity to punishment, while children with high/stabile CP but low CU traits show the opposite profile.

children with high CP and low CU (i.e. the non specifier group) and children with high CP high CU traits (i. e. the specifier group) score on opposite directions of fear and behavioral inhibition, and that children with high and stable CP low CU traits score on high behavioral inhibition and sensitivity to punishment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the heterogeneity of children with CP.
the identification and characterization of two distinct subtypes of children with CP.
the identification of the core characteristics of children with CP and CU traits and its implications for the understanding of developmental psychopathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of callous unemotionality in a group of children with high conduct problems is not a necessary condition for the emergence of fearlessness.
the two groups of antisocial children differ on the degree to which they exhibit fearlessness.
children high on both antisocial behavior and CU traits, are characterized by a deficit in fear, while children high on antisocial behavior but low on CU traits are characterized by high fear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the better of two evils is to exhibit low levels of fear, which may be a more protective factor than high fear.
children with high CP and low CU are more likely to be fearful and inhibited, and children with high CP/ high CU traits are less fearful and less inhibited.
children exhibiting high CP and low CU scores may be the most fearful and inhibited of all children, while those exhibiting high CP and high CU scores may be among the most fearless.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fearlessness is an important component of the psychopathological profile of children high on CP and CU traits.
the presence of callous unemotionality should not be considered a necessary condition to explain the presence of antisocial behavior in children.
children exhibiting high/stable CP, differentiated on CU traits, are qualitatively different in terms of fearlessness and behavioral inhibition.
